summary: The implementation matches the spec. sessionRecord/handWrite write `observed` only when counts are passed (D-3). It is built from nextHand(table), so a replaced bot gets no entry, and the counts that include the finished hand are always written beside handsPlayed = handNumber in one handWrite, so `hands <= handsPlayed` holds. The hook computes countObserved once, before the write (guarded by the `reported` ref), and passes that same object to handWrite (A-6). The ref starts from resume.observed, and App.resume calls restoreObserved inside its existing try/catch. parseSessionRecord checks a present `observed` after the seats, with the exact field names AC#2 asks for (`observed`, `observed[i]`, `.botId`, `.hands`, `.vpipHands`, `.pfrHands`), using isWhole with no coercion. Records without the field still parse and restore to {}. The tests would catch a broken implementation: SPEC-04 asserts exact RangeError messages plus findPausedSession rejection. SPEC-08 compares the stored `observed` with counts recomputed from the stored hand records and needs hands=3 after a real Resume, which would fail without the ref seeding. SPEC-03 checks every opponent line against the stored hands. On timeouts: in isolation the new Vitest files take about 1.4 s per 45-hand test (1.6 s for all four files). They are correctness tests, not speed or scale checks, so they belong in the normal suite. The 60_000 timeout follows the convention of 20+ existing acceptance files and is only headroom for coverage and parallel runs. Moving them to the slow group would wrongly take AC#1/AC#2 coverage out of every push. I did not run the e2e spec here; the build log reports the full e2e run passing. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
